SSR Performance's Project Leo Is a Twin-Turbo 911 GT3 RS With 911 GT2 RS Manthey Ambitions
14 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
One of the most exciting 911 specials yet, the 991 GT2 RS will soon gain an indirect successor based on the 992 GT3 RS. Enter the incredibly purposeful SSR Performance Project Leo, which is edging closer to production reality at the Green Hell. Just like Porsche's flagship 991, this fellow is an extreme interpretation of what the Neunelfer is supposed to be.
A simple glance at its rear quarter windows reveals that Munich-based SSR Performance had to rethink how the air moves into the engine compartment after giving the high-revving H6 a couple of snails. Large openings around the rear wheel arches can be seen as well, indicating very different cooling requirements from the naturally aspirated GT3 RS.
New vents are featured on top of the front fenders, and the front bumper wears double canards for improved aerodynamic stability. The aero-centric theme continues with a much larger front splitter, new skirts with altered intakes behind the doors, and the new diffuser out back.
Speaking of the rear end, the ginormous wing isn't the most dramatic element. Quad exhaust outlets that are facing the ground rather than the spy photographer suggest forced induction, and those four pipes make the rear end visually distinct from the dual center setup of the donor vehicle.
Back in April 2026, the German tuner and racing outfit published a teaser in which it described a proprietary high-performance cooling system for Project Leo. The rear side and bumper apertures are certainly part of the cooling-related changes, though it's too early to figure out the airflow target or the radiator layout.
Photo: SH Proshots Nevertheless, it sure is crazy to see how a turbo conversion of the GT3 RS has resulted in a comprehensive redesign of so many exterior panels and parts. The question is, how much power should we look forward to from Project Leo?
Porsche 's international website lists 525 ps and a top speed of 296 kph for the current GT3 RS, meaning 518 hp and 184 mph in American speak. Twin snails would result in 800 ponies at the very least, and with a bit of luck, Project Leo may be capable of exceeding 300 clicks on the Nurburgring's Dottinger Hohe.
As a brief refresher, the 991-generation GT2 RS offered 700 ps (690 hp) at full chatter and track speeds of up to 340 kph (211 mph). Regarding the current-gen GT3 RS, the biggest challenge to exceeding 300 clicks isn't power or gearing. It's aerodynamic drag, and SSR Performance needs to get it right if the company intends to smash the 911 GT2 RS Manthey's lap time at the Green Hell.
Speaking of Manthey, those disc-like wheels appear to be designed with aerodynamic efficiency and cooling in mind. A bespoke transmission application was confirmed by SSR, though it's not clear whether the company is developing on the PDK or uses a motorsport-infused sequential unit.
Expected to lap the Ring in less than 7 minutes, Project Leo has to prove itself against the 991 GT2 RS Manthey. It will be tremendously difficult, though. The Manthey-prepped 911 GT2 RS from the 991 generation blitzed the German circuit in 6:43.3 in 2021, whereas the Mercedes-AMG ONE hypercar required 6:29.090 to complete the full 20.8-kilometer lap.
